readout_other: self-reported type/location of tactile sensations; touch-sensor tap response indicating sensation timing
direction_notes: FUS to SI, SII, or SI+SII simultaneously elicited tactile sensations (e.g. tingling, weak electrical current, numbness) from the hand/arm contralateral to sonication in most subjects, with no sensations reported during sham; stimulation of specific SII sub-regions did not reliably elicit the corresponding sensation-specific percept, indicating an excitatory but not finely spatially-selective effect.
safety_notes: Neurological examination and MMSE before/after sonication and at follow-up (same day, 2 weeks, 4 weeks) showed no abnormal findings; telephone follow-up at 8 weeks reported no discomfort or mental/physical changes. Estimated in-situ intensity (7.0-8.8 W/cm2 Isppa, 3.5-4.4 W/cm2 Ispta) was slightly above the IEC 60601 part 2 Ispta limit of 3 W/cm2 but below intensities (up to 13.4 W/cm2 Isppa in situ) previously found not to cause microscopic brain damage in sheep; estimated temperature rise was 0.0092 degC.

exposures.label: SI_FUS: stimulation of primary somatosensory cortex alone

target.label: primary somatosensory area (SI) of the hand

device.model: single-element FUS transducer, 210 kHz, 30 mm outer diameter, 25 mm focal distance

timing.protocol_description: FUS procedures were divided into multiple sessions: (1) SI alone (SI_FUS), (2) four sub-regions of SII (SII_FUS), (3) simultaneous SI and SII (SI/SII_FUS), and (4) sham (Sham_FUS, same setup without sonication); condition order was randomized and balanced across subjects. Sonication was administered 20 times per session/sub-region. Participants tapped a touch sensor to report sensation timing and verbally reported location/type of sensation after each condition; both subject and operator were blinded to the nature of the sonication.

exposures.label: SII_FUS: stimulation of secondary somatosensory cortex sub-regions (vibrotactile, pressure, warmth, coolness)

device.model: single-element FUS transducer, 210 kHz, 30 mm outer diameter, 25 mm focal distance

timing.protocol_description: FUS procedures were divided into multiple sessions: (1) SI alone (SI_FUS), (2) four sub-regions of SII corresponding to vibrotactile, pressure, warmth and coolness representations (SII_FUS), (3) simultaneous SI and SII (SI/SII_FUS), and (4) sham (Sham_FUS, same setup without sonication); condition order was randomized and balanced across subjects. Sonication was administered 20 times per session/sub-region. Participants tapped a touch sensor to report sensation timing and verbally reported location/type of sensation after each condition; both subject and operator were blinded to the nature of the sonication.

flags.reason: The FUS procedure comprised multiple within-day condition blocks per subject (SI alone; four SII sub-regions; four SI/SII sub-regions; sham), each given 20 times, but the paper does not state a single 'number of sessions per subject'; left not_reported rather than computed by counting condition blocks.

In-situ intensity is an estimate (not per-subject simulation or measurement) based on a previously reported average transcranial transmission rate of 20-25%, given as a range (7.0-8.8 W/cm2 Isppa); the midpoint (7.9) is recorded per schema convention and the quote carries the full range.

In the SI/SII_FUS condition both SI and SII were sonicated simultaneously with two independent transducers using the same parameters; this combined condition is captured in protocol_description under both the SI and SII exposures rather than as a separate exposure, since the target/frequency pairs are unchanged.
